title: How the Camel Got His Hump
blurb: A camel refuses to work and says only one word: humph.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… when the world was still brand new, and the animals were only just beginning to work for people, there was a Camel.

[amused] He lived right in the middle of a howling desert, because he did not WANT to work. [playfully] And he ate sticks, and thorns, and prickly things… and when anybody spoke to him, he said one word, and one word only.

[firmly] “Humph.”

[curious] On Monday morning, the Horse came to him with a saddle on his back.

[warmly] “Camel, O Camel,” said the Horse, “come and trot with us.”

[annoyed] “Humph,” said the Camel. And the Horse went away and told the Man.

[curious] On Tuesday, the Dog came to him with a stick in his mouth.

[warmly] “Camel, O Camel, come and fetch and carry with us.”

[annoyed] “Humph,” said the Camel.

[curious] And on Wednesday, the Ox came with a yoke on his neck. “Camel, O Camel, come and plough with us.”

[annoyed] “Humph,” said the Camel. [short pause] And that was all he ever said.

[firmly] At the end of the day, the Man called the three of them together.

[sad] “I am sorry,” he said, “but that Camel cannot work. So you three must work twice as hard, to make up for him.”

[worried] That made the Horse very angry, and the Dog very angry, and the Ox very angry. [thoughtful] And they went off to the edge of the desert to talk about it.

[softly] Now while they were talking, along came the Djinn who was in charge of All Deserts, rolling in a cloud of dust.

[curious] “Djinn of All Deserts,” they said, “is it right for anyone to be idle, with the world so new?”

[firmly] “Certainly not,” said the Djinn. “Who is it?”

[annoyed] “A thing with three legs and a long neck,” said the Horse, “who says humph.”

[calmly] So the Djinn rolled away across the sand, and found the Camel looking at his own reflection in a pool.

[gently] “My friend,” said the Djinn, “I hear you are doing no work at all.”

[annoyed] “Humph,” said the Camel.

[amused] “I should not say that again, if I were you,” said the Djinn. “You have missed three whole days.”

[firmly] “Humph,” said the Camel.

[surprised] And the moment he said it, his back began to puff, and to swell, and to rise… [short pause] until there sat upon it one great big lolloping humph. [amused] Though we have learned to say hump, so as not to hurt his feelings.

[gently] “Now,” said the Djinn, “you can work for three days without eating, because you can live off your humph.”

[warmly] And the Camel went out to join the other three. [short pause] And from that day to this, he has carried his humph upon his back — and he has never yet caught up on those three missed days.
